become.definition: To begin to be or turn into something.
examples: He becomes angry when plans change.
She became a lawyer last year.
It has become very cold outside.

begin.definition: To start or initiate an action.
examples: The class begins at nine o'clock every morning.
It began to rain heavily an hour ago.
We have begun our new project.

come.definition: To move towards or arrive at a place.
examples: He comes home at six PM every day.
She came to visit us last weekend.
My parents have come to stay with us.
She drinks two liters of water daily.
He drank a glass of milk before bed.
We have drunk all the orange juice.
She finds good deals online.
He found his missing keys under the sofa.
We have found a solution to the problem.

hold.definition: To grasp or support with hands.
examples: She holds the baby gently.
He held the door open for everyone.
They have held the event annually.

meet.definition: To encounter or assemble with someone.
examples: She meets her friends every weekend.
He met the director yesterday morning.
We have met before at a conference.

read.definition: To look at and comprehend written text.
examples: He reads the newspaper every morning.
She read three books last month.
I have read that novel twice.

ring.definition: To make a clear resonant sound.
examples: The phone rings loudly in the hall.
He rang the doorbell twice.
The church bell has rung twelve times.
He runs five kilometers every morning.
She ran to catch the train.
They have run two marathons this year.

sing.definition: To produce musical sounds with the voice.
examples: She sings in the church choir.
He sang a beautiful song at the party.
They have sung that hymn together.

sit.definition: To rest weight on buttocks or seat.
examples: He sits near the window in class.
She sat on the bench in the park.
We have sat here for an hour.
She swims in the pool every morning.
He swam across the lake easily.
They have swum in the ocean.

win.definition: To achieve victory in a contest.
examples: He wins matches consistently.
She won first prize in the competition.
They have won three awards.
The contract binds both parties legally.
He bound the package with strong rope.
They have bound the documents together.
A small cut bleeds slightly.
His nose bled after he fell.
The wound has bled through the bandage.
He breeds racehorses on his farm.
They bred sheep for wool for generations.
They have bred high-quality cattle.

cling.definition: To hold on tightly or adhere.
examples: The wet shirt clings to his back.
The child clung to her mother's coat.
They have clung to old traditions.

dig.definition: To break up and turn earth.
examples: The dog digs holes in the garden.
He dug a deep trench for the pipes.
They have dug a new well.
She feeds her cat every morning.
He fed the horses in the barn.
They have fed the hungry visitors.
She hangs her coat on the hook.
He hung a painting on the living room wall.
They have hung decorations outside.

lead.definition: To guide or conduct along a way.
examples: The tour guide leads the group.
She led the team to a great victory.
He has led the organization well.
She lights a candle every evening.
He lit the fireplace when it got cold.
They have lit up the entire street.

overcome.definition: To succeed in dealing with problem/fear.
examples: She overcomes obstacles with determination.
He overcame his fear of heights.
They have overcome great hardship.
The sun shines brightly today.
His flashlight shone through the dark.
Her eyes have shone with joy.

shoot.definition: To fire a weapon or film a scene.
examples: He shoots arrows at the target.
The photographer shot great pictures.
They have shot a new documentary.

sink.definition: To submerge or go beneath surface.
examples: A heavy stone sinks in water.
The boat sank during the storm.
The sun has sunk below the horizon.

slide.definition: To glide smoothly along a surface.
examples: Children slide down the icy hill.
The glass slid off the smooth table.
He has slid into third base.

speed.definition: To move at high speed or hurry.
examples: The ambulance speeds through traffic.
He sped past the radar checkpoint.
The train has sped away.

spit.definition: To eject saliva or liquid from mouth.
examples: The camel spits when annoyed.
He spat out the bitter medicine.
He has spat on the ground.

spring.definition: To leap, jump, or arise suddenly.
examples: Grass springs up after warm rain.
He sprang up from his chair.
A new idea has sprung to mind.
Glue sticks paper together well.
The key stuck in the old lock.
We have stuck to our original plan.

sting.definition: To wound with a sharp organ/stinger.
examples: A bee stings when threatened.
A wasp stung him on his arm.
The insect has stung her leg.

strike.definition: To hit sharply or deliver blow.
examples: Clock strikes twelve at midnight.
Lightning struck the tall tower.
Disaster has struck the small town.

swing.definition: To sway or move back and forth.
examples: The pendulum swings continuously.
He swung the bat and hit the ball.
The gate has swung wide open.
The mill grinds wheat into flour.
He ground coffee beans fresh morning.
The pepper has been ground finely.

outrun.definition: To run faster or further than.
examples: The cheetah outruns its prey easily.
He outran the defender to score.
They have outrun the police car.
Wool shrinks in hot water washes.
The sweater shrank after washing.
Market demand has shrunk lately.
He slings backpack over shoulder.
She slung stone across river bank.
The hammock was slung between trees.
Thief slinks through narrow alley.
He slunk away from accusation scene.
The shadow has slunk into alley.
Garbage stinks in hot summer.
The room stank of stale smoke.
The sewer pipe has stunk all day.
She unwinds by reading novels.
He unwound long garden hose pipe.
He has unwound after hard day.

withhold.definition: To refuse to give or hold back.
examples: Company withhold tax from salary.
He withheld vital information court.
They have withheld payment details.

alight.definition: To step down or land upon.
examples: A bird alights on tree branch.
Passengers alit from train platform.
The falcon has alit on roof.
She dives off high springboard.
He dove into cold ocean waves.
They have dived for sunken treasures.
False ads mislead consumers easily.
The map misled hikers into woods.
Public has been misled by claims.
Cliff overhangs stormy sea below.
Branches overhung narrow forest trail.
Roof has overhung balcony deck.

overrun.definition: To swarm over or exceed limit.
examples: Weeds overrun neglected gardens.
Enemy forces overran border post.
Budget has overrun initial estimate.

overshoot.definition: To shoot or pass beyond target.
examples: Plane overshoots runway landing.
Pilot overshot runway in heavy fog.
Target metrics have been overshot.

rebind.definition: To bind again or bounce back.
examples: Prices rebound after drop.
Stock market rebounded quickly today.
Economy has rebound from slump.
He rewinds video cassette tape.
She rewound film to start scene.
Tape has been rewound completely.

string.definition: To thread on cord or tune guitar.
examples: She strings beads into necklace.
He strung guitar with new wire.
Lights have been strung on trees.

wring.definition: To extract money or truth by force.
examples: Interrogator wrings confession from suspect.
He wrung promise from reluctant partner.
Truth was wrung from him.
